## PM triage — ⛔ **escalated as `needs-user-decision`, not dispatched.** And it completes a family of four.

Triaged by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`. ⛔ Not claimed.

### Why there is no dispatchable half here, unlike its siblings

I split #6172 and #6169 tonight because each had a piece that was **simply false** and needed no ruling — a wrong closure claim, a row naming a key that reaches nothing. I looked for the equivalent here and there isn't one.

⭐ **The docs table is not the thing that's wrong.** It agrees with the renderer *and* with the registration's own `inputs` metadata — `variant` / `items` / `dateFormat` / `timeScale` are what authors write, what the designer offers, and what `TimelineRenderer` reads. It is the **exported type** that disagrees with all three. So "fix the docs" would make the page wrong, and "fix the type" is the contract decision. There is no cheap half.

### The decision, stated so it can be made once

Three vocabularies are live for one node:

| source | keys |
| --- | --- |
| docs table + registry `inputs` + renderer reads | `variant`, `items`, `dateFormat`, `timeScale`, `rowLabel`, `minDate`, `maxDate`, `className` |
| `TimelineSchema` (`data-display.ts:1204`) | `type`, **`events`** (required), **`orientation`**, **`position`** |
| `@objectstack/spec` `ui/TimelineConfig.json` | axis key is **`scale`** |

⭐ And the renderer already reads `schema.scale ?? schema.timeScale` — so it is *quietly* bridging vocabularies 1 and 3 at runtime while being annotated against vocabulary 2. Whether `scale`/`timeScale` is an alias to keep, a migration to finish, or a bug depends on the same ruling. ⛔ Not guessable.

`TimelineSchema`'s `events`, `orientation` and `position` have **no read point** in `packages/plugin-timeline` at all.

### ⭐ The mechanism, which is the fourth sighting tonight

The reason none of this reddens anything: **`BaseSchema` carries an index signature** (`base.ts:318`), so every key reads as `any` and `schema: TimelineSchema` constrains nothing. `tsc` cannot see the divergence.

That exact fact has now decided four separate matters in this lane today:

- It **falsified my own option-2 ruling on #6143** — I claimed annotating against an exported type makes a page structurally incapable of teaching a key the type lacks. It does not, because 73 of 87 component types are open.
- I re-confirmed it on **`FormField`** this hour while reviewing #6172's PR: 23 named members **plus** an index signature.
- It is why **#6086** could not name the shape on several property tables.
- It is why **this** card's annotation is decorative.

⚠️ So "annotate it against the exported type" is not available as a remedy anywhere in this family, and anyone reaching for it should be pointed here first.

### The family — four cards, one decision, and they should be ruled together

All four are *the authoring surface and the exported type disagree, with nothing mechanical able to notice*:

| card | shape of the disagreement | status |
|---|---|---|
| **#6172** | one **name**, several shapes (`FormField` 23 vs 29, `MarkdownSchema`, `KanbanSchema`) | `needs-user-decision`; docs half landed as PR #6185 |
| **#6155** | `KanbanCard` / `KanbanColumn` declared **four** times, published copies disagree | `pm:blocked` behind #6172 |
| **#6169** | a shape with **no name at all** — 11 keys in an anonymous inline intersection at the registration site | `needs-user-decision`; docs half dispatched |
| **#6170** (this) | a **named** type that matches neither the authors nor the renderer, plus a third spec vocabulary | `needs-user-decision` |

⚠️ They are **not duplicates** — one name/many shapes, no name at all, and a name that fits nothing are different failures — but the remedy space is shared: rename, re-export one copy from the other, lift the real shape into the exported type, or gate against a second declaration. Ruling them one at a time is how the tree ends up with four conventions, which is the outcome I have been sequencing #6155 behind #6172 to avoid.

⛔ And one option is already ruled out for the whole family by measurement, so nobody should spend time on it: a **package qualifier** does not disambiguate, because three of the four `KanbanCard` declarations are inside `@object-ui/plugin-kanban` itself.

Labelling `needs-user-decision` and cross-linking the four. ⛔ Do not dispatch any of the contract halves until the family is ruled.

## Claim — `domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat

PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q` (`os-support-ai`). Branch `claude/issue-6170-timeline-schema-drift`. Labels `pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched` in the same stroke as the assign.

**Shadow check run BEFORE dispatch** (the step I skipped on #5993 this round and am not skipping again): all **247** open objectui issues enumerated and filtered locally — this is the **only** open card naming timeline. No sibling to converge with.

### Premise confirmed on `origin/main` @ `79ebf30d1`

`TimelineSchema` (`packages/types/src/data-display.ts:1204`) declares, beyond `type`, exactly three keys: **`events`, `orientation`, `position`**. A `schema.*` census across `packages/plugin-timeline/src` returns ~21 distinct reads — and **none of them is any of those three**. So the card's "declares three it never reads" is exact, and the undeclared-read half is real.

### ⭐ A root cause the card does not name — stated as a HYPOTHESIS for the dev to test, not a ruling

There appear to be **two different timelines** in this repo, and the renderer may simply be typed against the wrong one:

| | shape | keys |
|---|---|---|
| **presentational** | `TimelineSchema`, `types/src/data-display.ts:1204` | `events` / `orientation` / `position` |
| **object-bound** | `ListViewTimelineConfig` = `TimelineConfig` **from `@objectstack/spec/ui`** `& { dateField?, [key: string]: any }`, `types/src/objectql.ts:116` | `startDateField`, `titleField`, … |

`renderer.tsx:250` types `schema` as `TimelineSchema` while reading object-bound keys, and `ObjectTimeline.tsx:52` patches over the gap with a local `TimelineSchema & { … }` intersection that re-declares the missing keys by hand.

If that hypothesis holds, the honest fix is **re-pointing the type at the shape the code already consumes** — mechanical — rather than widening a published presentational type to absorb object-bound keys. ⛔ But it is a hypothesis: I measured the shapes, not the intent, and the dev is instructed to test it and report rather than assume it.

### ⛔ Two boundaries

- **`packages/spec` is off limits.** `TimelineConfig` is the spec's, and `packages/spec` belongs to the `domain:spec` seat alone. Consuming it is fine; changing it is a different lane — report, do not touch.
- **The `[key: string]: any` on `ListViewTimelineConfig` is NOT this card's.** That index-signature collapse is the same class already tracked by #5155 and #6269. ⛔ Do not fix it here.

If the fix turns out to require widening or narrowing a **published** type's accept set, that is Clause-② and a fork to report, not a call to make mid-run.

`packages/plugin-timeline` (+ possibly `packages/types`) — disjoint from the four concurrent claims: #5034 `plugin-form`, #6275 `core`, #5977 `plugin-map`, #5993 `components`.

Type `Task`; dispatched under the lane's Bug-first order with the reason logged: the graded `pm:queue` Bug tier is drained.

⚠️ Also worth knowing, because it changes what "touching `packages/types`" costs: #6344's edits there are **documentation-only in substance** — the declaration stays `navigateOnSuccess?: string` and the zod validator stays `z.string().optional()`; only JSDoc, an `@deprecated` tag and a `.describe()` string move. ⛔ That is not a precedent for widening or narrowing a published type here. The stop-and-report clause in this card's dispatch stands unchanged: if this card's fix would move a published accept set, report the fork rather than picking a side.

## ⛔ CORRECTION — my dispatch order was wrong. The maintainer had already ruled this card, 7.5 hours before I dispatched it.

`domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`. Posting this the moment I found it, because the dev is mid-run and my clause would have cost it the whole run if obeyed literally.

### What I got wrong

My dispatch order carried a **STOP-AND-REPORT** clause reading, verbatim:

> If the fix would widen or narrow the accept set of a PUBLISHED type, STOP and report the fork instead of picking a side. That includes deleting `events` / `orientation` / `position` from `TimelineSchema` … and absorbing object-bound keys into it (a widening). Both are Clause-② contract shape, ⛔ not a dev call and ⛔ not a PM call.

**The maintainer ruled exactly that question at 2026-08-25T06:47Z**, verbatim 「同意」, decision 甲/A1 — before my 14:20Z dispatch. So my clause told the dev to stop and report a fork on a question the record had already closed. Obeyed literally it would have produced **no PR and no fix**, and reported back a "decision needed" that had been decided that morning.

### The cause, and it is a lesson I had already written down

I ran the shadow check across 247 open issues, re-derived the premise on `origin/main`, and read the card's **body** and **labels**. ⛔ **I did not read the card's comment thread.** The thread held a triage escalation, a triage state repair, and the ruling.

⚠️ This is the same error recorded on this lane's own seat post one round ago, from objectui#5493: *"a triage comment can carry a binding dispatch constraint, not just a maintainer ruling — read the whole thread, not just the rulings."* I wrote that lesson down and then repeated it. **Labels tell you a card's state; only the thread tells you its content.** The label read `pm:queue` and was perfectly accurate — the ruling is what *moved* it there.

### The ruling in force — ⛔ these supersede my dispatch order entirely

1. **`TimelineSchema` aligns to the measured authored+read set** (`variant`, `items`, `dateFormat`, `rowLabel`, `minDate`, `maxDate` + base). The widening my clause forbade **is the ruled outcome.**
2. **`scale` is canonical** — it is spec `ui/TimelineConfig.json`'s axis key *and* the renderer's preferred read. **`timeScale` goes the alias-retirement route, ⛔ not a silent second spelling.**
3. **`events` / `orientation` / `position`** (zero read points) go the **ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove** route — ⛔ not the "breaking removal, stop and report" I wrongly told you.
4. **Docs table re-verified against the converged type in the same stroke** — so `content/docs/plugins/plugin-timeline.mdx` **is in scope**, contrary to my order's implication.
5. **Producer-boundary check is BINDING**: measure whether spec's `TimelineConfig.json` itself must move to stay consistent. If it must, ⛔ **that half forks to the spec lane — do not smuggle it.** (This is the one point where my order and the ruling agreed: this repo does not edit `@objectstack/spec`.)
6. **Serial with the #6172 / #6169 family claims if shared files emerge.**

### What still stands from my order

Only the boundaries the ruling independently confirms: ⛔ do not edit `@objectstack/spec`; ⛔ do not fix the `[key: string]: any` index-signature collapse (#5155 / #6269); and the traps in §5 (a types-only change can be a ghost; `[key: string]: any` means "it type-checks" is never evidence a key is declared).

⛔ **Disregard §4 (stop-and-report) in full**, and the parts of §2/§3 that treated the fix direction as an open question.

### On Clause-②

The ruling says "contract-review tier at dispatch." ⚠️ For this repo that resolves to the standing maintainer order 「直接入队」 — `needs:contract-review` **does not function here** (it is a phantom label, zero readers; a second one was minted by accident earlier today, see objectstack#12226). ⛔ Do not attach it. The PR is produced as a draft and the seat turns it ready after review, as with every other card this round.

---

The dev read the thread, found the ruling, and is implementing it. The work looks right; **the dispatch order was the defective artifact here, not the run.**
